target_pattern: Use three future frames naturally: ir a plus infinitive, present plus future time, and simple future, while recognizing irregular future stems and the supposition use of future tense.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Using only going to translations and avoiding Spanish future forms.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Spanish uses three future paths naturally and uses simple future also for probability guesses.
target_pattern_formula: ir conjugated plus a plus infinitive
present tense plus future time expression
simple future: infinitive plus e, as, a, emos, an
irregular stems: tendr, dir, har, saldr, vendr, habr

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as instructed.
drills: Base: Hablare con Maria. -> change subject to nosotros.
Base: Voy a estudiar manana. -> change to simple future.
Base: Trabajo el sabado. -> change day to el lunes.
Base: Ellos llegaran tarde. -> make it a yes/no question.
Base: El saldra temprano. -> make it negative.
Base: Tendremos reunion a las nueve. -> change to singular yo form.
Base: La empresa abrira una oficina en junio. -> change subject to plural empresas.
Base: Veremos los resultados el viernes. -> change object to singular el resultado.
Base: Voy a enviar el informe ahora. -> change subject to ella.
Base: Estara en casa. -> change to question form.
Base: Tendran unos cuarenta anos. -> change estimate to thirty.
Base: Dire la verdad manana. -> change subject to tu.
Base: Vendremos el domingo. -> change to ellos.
Base: Hara calor manana. -> change to question form.
Base: Acabamos la presentacion el martes. -> rewrite with simple future.

contrastive_discrimination.instructions: Choose the most natural Spanish option for the intended meaning.
prompts: I will call you tonight. (Te llamare esta noche. vs Te voy a llamare esta noche.)
We are going to travel tomorrow. (Vamos a viajar manana. vs Viajaremos a manana.)
I work tomorrow. (Trabajo manana. vs Trabajare manana.)
Will you bring me another napkin, please? (Me traes otra servilleta, por favor? vs Me traerás otra servilleta, por favor?)
He is probably at home. (Estara en casa. vs Esta en casa probablemente.)
Who might that be? (Quien sera? vs Quien esra?)
They will have more time. (Tendran mas tiempo. vs Teneran mas tiempo.)
She will say it tomorrow. (Lo dira manana. vs Lo decira manana.)
We will leave early. (Saldremos temprano. vs Saliremos temprano.)
I am going to study tonight. (Voy a estudiar esta noche. vs Voy estudiar esta noche.)

common_errors.why_it_happens: Mixing two future patterns in one verb slot.

common_errors.mistake: Teneran or decira or salira with regular stems
common_errors.why_it_happens: Treating irregulars as regular infinitive stems.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Use irregular stems: tendran, dira, saldra.

common_errors.why_it_happens: Omitting a in ir a plus infinitive.

common_errors.mistake: Me traeras otra servilleta, por favor?
common_errors.why_it_happens: Literal English will you polite request transfer.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Me traes otra servilleta, por favor?

common_errors.why_it_happens: Overgeneralizing sera or estara guessing use.

common_errors.mistake: Missing question marks in future questions
common_errors.correct_spanish: Use opening and closing question marks.

common_errors.mistake: Avoiding present plus time as future
common_errors.why_it_happens: Belief that only formal future is correct.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Present plus future time is common and natural.
